responses.evidence: Confirmed gap in assembleFactoryStatus run/controller assembly (factory-status.ts): factory_run_id/loop_run_id/contract_hash/engine_pin are OR-merged from macro, loop, process, and pin without equality checks, so contradictory active run or contract identities can form one false snapshot. Revised d1: pure assembler gains explicit correlation keys (loop_run_id/process run_id, contract/canonical hashes, factory_run_id, process boot binding), precedence by source role when consistent, and degraded source_identity_conflict behavior that refuses to blend mismatched subsets; injected tests required for match, mismatched run, and mismatched contract.

Key allowlisting alone is insufficient: mode, service_controller, run ids, contract hashes, fingerprints, operation ids, advance_run_id, hostname, and lock staleness currently pass typeof===string checks (factory-status.ts assembly) while canary fixtures only seed forbidden token/prompt fields. Revised d3: every emitted scalar must be a closed enum, validated identifier/fingerprint, finite number, or parseable ISO timestamp; validators cover controller/service identity, revision, contract/run ids, fingerprints, item stage/links, and attribution details; canary matrix must inject canaries into every public-capable scalar source field and prove absence from JSON, prose, and errors.

Confirmed race: startIndependentHeartbeat does const next={...base, heartbeat_at} then writeProcess(next) while markControllerOperation concurrently writes a full updated record (supervisor.ts / factory-status.ts). A delayed heartbeat can restore stale operation/wait/progress or revive post-terminal state. Revised d4: monotonic record_version (or CAS generation), identity-bound heartbeat merge that only patches heartbeat_at on matching run_id+boot_id+token non-terminal records, rebase-on-version-move, terminal/lock-loss no-op, and interleaving tests for delayed/reordered heartbeat vs dispatch/wait/failure/terminal.

Prior d4 required a durable failure marker but did not specify schema, controller/run/boot binding, write ordering, expiry, or recovery clear — so an old marker could degrade a replacement controller. Revised d4 failure-marker contract: allowlisted schema with run_id+boot_id+hostname+pid+failed_at+error_code; honor only when bound to the observed identity; clear/supersede on successful same-identity write; ignore other boot_ids and markers older than a newer successful heartbeat_at; restart tests for stale marker vs recovered persistence.

Prior d5 matrix still allowed stale+pid-absent+no service -> dead. That falsely declares an unmanaged same-host restart dead when a replacement controller holds the same run. Revised d5: public dead is recorded-identity death (detail recorded_identity_absent), not global factory absence; replacement evidence (lock holder different pid/boot for same run, fresher process identity, active service) forces unknown; unmanaged pid-absent dead only when no replacement evidence is present.

Macro health ownership was only a generalization_boundary note (adopt heartbeat when #890 owns the run) without a falsifiable writer interface or explicit unknown fallback — status could not prove macro-as-driver health and might over-trust identity fields. Revised d6+d8: shared ControllerHealthEvidenceWriter (heartbeat merge, mark operation/wait, failure marker); loop supervisor implements now; hybrid macro-identity + loop writer is supported; exclusive macro drive MUST implement the writer with injected integration-style tests; macro without processIdentity writer evidence => liveness/operation/wait are legacy/unknown, never healthy from identity alone.

decisions.title: Pure allowlisted assembler over injected readers with explicit multi-source correlation
decisions.surface: core/scripts/factory-status.ts (`assembleFactoryStatus`, `FactoryStatusSources`, `FactoryStatusProbes`, `FactoryStatusClock`, source-correlation helper); CLI wiring in core/scripts/pipeline.ts; OpenSpec design Decision 1

alternatives.option: Persist a second durable factory-status ledger that status writes and re-reads
alternatives.rejected_because: Acceptance requires zero mutation of ledger/events/run artifacts; a write path would make status a control surface and couple observability to a new durable schema.

alternatives.option: Expose the raw loop-store status projection as the remote/CLI contract
alternatives.rejected_because: Loop status and supervisor records include lock tokens and unbounded free text; issue non-goals forbid shipping raw loop status over remote-safe surfaces.

alternatives.option: Merge every present source field by independent per-field precedence without run/contract correlation (prior d1)
alternatives.rejected_because: Contradictory macro/loop/process/pin/provider inputs can be stitched into one false active contract/run snapshot; challenge 8e098cf4 requires explicit correlation or degraded conflict.

assumptions: Existing controller/process, loop status, pin, provider, write-health, and cost sources can be projected through injected seams without live network/git/subprocess in unit tests.
CLI is responsible only for mapping filesystem/config into seams and printing the envelope.
Correlation keys are available as plain identifiers on the injected sources (run_id, contract/canonical hash, factory_run_id, process boot_id) without status mutation.
invariants: `assembleFactoryStatus` is pure: no GitHub, git, service, control, ledger, event, or run-artifact mutation.
Unit tests inject clocks, process probes, and source objects; no real network/git/subprocess.

Correlation keys (when present): `loop_run_id` / process `run_id`, `contract_hash` / loop `canonical_hash` / macro `linked_runs.loop_contract_hash` / macro `canonical_hash`, optional `factory_run_id`, and process identity binding (`hostname`,`pid`,`boot_id`) for the live driver.

Precedence when consistent: processIdentity is authoritative for liveness/operation/wait/progress; loopStatus is authoritative for item rows and loop run_id/engine when present; macroController is authoritative for factory_run_id, mode, revision, service identity, coarse_phase, and macro fingerprints; pin is authoritative for engine_pin when macro pin fingerprint is absent; provider is authoritative for cooldown.

Conflict rule: if any two present correlation keys disagree on the same dimension (mismatched loop_run_id across macro.linked_runs / loopStatus / processIdentity; mismatched contract_hash across macro / loop; process.run_id vs loop.run_id), the envelope MUST NOT blend the mismatched subsets into one active snapshot. Top-level `status` becomes `degraded`, a structured allowlisted conflict code is recorded (e.g. sources attribution / detail code `source_identity_conflict`), and for each conflicted dimension the assembler emits null/unknown for the blended field set rather than picking a silent winner that invents a false joint contract/run.
Health classification still runs on the processIdentity-bound subset when that source is present and self-consistent; it does not borrow operation/wait from a run_id-mismatched peer.

Injected-source tests cover: matching keys -> single coherent snapshot; mismatched active run ids -> degraded conflict without false merge; mismatched contract hashes -> degraded conflict; pin-only disagreement does not invent run identity but may degrade pin attribution only.
evidence: Prior assembly (factory-status.ts run block) used OR-precedence across macro/loop/proc without equality checks — revised by this decision.
core/scripts/factory-status.ts module header: pure function over injected sources/clock/probes.
openspec/changes/factory-aggregate-status-and-controller-health/design.md Decision 1 intent (pure assembler); correlation is additive to purity, not a second ledger.
decisions.generalization_boundary: Does not replace scoreboard (#301), per-issue status (#154), audit logs, or run artifacts; does not implement HTTP/MCP exposure of the raw store. Correlation is observational only — no auto-repair of source stores.
decisions.uncertainty: Low for purity requirement (acceptance-bound). Medium that #890 will always populate linked_runs.loop_run_id/contract when both macro and loop are live; falsified if production routinely omits link fields while both run — then conflict detection must treat missing links as unknown rather than conflict.

decisions.title: Versioned envelope with ok/degraded/error and additive v1 fields

alternatives.option: Throw unstructured stderr-only failures for machine consumers
alternatives.rejected_because: Acceptance requires exactly one unfenced versioned JSON object including structured error/degraded states parseable via `JSON.parse(stdout)`.

alternatives.option: Bump schema_version on every additive optional field
alternatives.rejected_because: Design allows optional/unknown-safe additives within schema_version "1" so legacy and partial sources stay readable without forcing consumer version churn.

assumptions: Partial source failure should surface as degraded with per-source attribution rather than look fully healthy.
Total assembly failure still emits a valid error envelope.
Source identity conflicts (d1) use degraded, not hard error, when a partial consistent subset remains readable.
invariants: `schema_version` is the string `"1"` for this contract.
Top-level `status` is exactly `ok` | `degraded` | `error`.
Missing optional sources are attributed (`unknown` / `legacy` / `not_applicable` / `error`), not silently invented as healthy presence.
Top-level `error` (when present) is an allowlisted error code only — never residual free text (see d3).
evidence: core/scripts/factory-status.ts: `FACTORY_STATUS_SCHEMA_VERSION = "1"`, `FactoryStatusTopLevel`, forceError error-envelope path.
openspec/changes/factory-aggregate-status-and-controller-health/design.md Decision 2.
core/test/factory-status.test.ts: error/degraded envelope and missing-source attribution tests.
decisions.generalization_boundary: Additive optional fields stay on v1 only while they remain optional/unknown-safe; breaking renames or required new fields need a schema bump.
decisions.uncertainty: Low. Falsified if a consumer needs a hard break (required new field with no unknown default) without a version change.

decisions.title: Allowlist-built public envelope; every emitted scalar is enum, validated id/fingerprint, number, or timestamp; errors are allowlisted codes only
decisions.surface: core/scripts/factory-status.ts (public key allowlist, closed enums, per-field scalar validators, `mapFactoryStatusErrorCode`, `projectLoopSourcesForFactoryStatus`); canary suite in core/test/factory-status.test.ts covering every public-capable scalar source field; CLI catch path in core/scripts/pipeline.ts

alternatives.option: Regex/denylist redaction alone over the raw loop status JSON
alternatives.rejected_because: Denylist is incomplete against new secret shapes and free-text prompt injection; acceptance requires an explicit allowlist and canary proof that secrets and instruction-like text never appear.

alternatives.option: Pass through issue titles, hold reasons, comments, and next-action prose for operator richness
alternatives.rejected_because: Remote-safe contract forbids unsanitized issue/comment/reason text and instruction-like free text in JSON, prose, and error paths.

alternatives.option: Allowlist top-level/nested keys only and pass raw strings for mode, revision strings, run ids, fingerprints, stages, links, and attribution details (prior partial d3)
alternatives.rejected_because: Key allowlisting does not make allowed scalar values safe; canaries in public-capable source scalars can still appear in JSON/human output (challenge 47297690).

alternatives.option: Cap and denylist-redact thrown error messages into the public `error` field
alternatives.rejected_because: Residual free text after partial redaction still can carry canaries or prompt-like instructions; remote-safe contract requires fixed allowlisted error codes only.

assumptions: Operators can obtain rich free text from existing audit/logs/status surfaces; factory status is the coarse remote-safe projection.
Registered source keys and every public-capable scalar field on those sources must receive canary fixtures.
A closed set of factory-status error codes is sufficient for machine consumers; operators use logs for exception detail.
invariants: Only named public fields are assembled; source objects are never dumped wholesale onto the envelope.
Lock/bearer tokens, credentials, secret refs, env maps, prompts, tool dumps, and raw supervisor token fields never copy into the public model.

Projection table for every emitted scalar: (1) closed enum (status, health states, wait kinds, next_action codes, attribution, cost coverage, host_class, controller.kind, item state, coarse health, error codes, wait/operation detail codes); (2) validated identifier/fingerprint matching a tight pattern (e.g. run/item/contract/engine/pin/service/mode/stage/fingerprint/candidate: printable token class with max length; reject otherwise -> null/unknown); (3) finite numeric (revision, pid, pr, counts, usd) with type/range checks; (4) parseable ISO-8601 timestamp or null. No other free-text residual.

Controller/service identity, revision, contract/run identifiers, fingerprints, item stage/link fields, lock staleness codes, write_health summary, operation ids, and source-attribution detail codes all pass through the validators above — not only next_action, wait-kind, and error.
Public error surfaces emit only allowlisted error codes — never source exception messages or redacted residual free text.
Source `{ __error }` inputs map through the same code allowlist; raw `__error` strings never appear in JSON/human/stderr.

Canary matrix covers: every source key; every public-capable scalar source field (mode, service_controller, run ids, hashes, fingerprints, stage, advance_run_id, candidate, operation id, hostnames, staleness, summaries, timestamps filled with canary strings); forceError paths; CLI catch-before-assembly; canaries at start/middle/end of adversarial exception strings. Proof: no canary appears in JSON.stringify(envelope), human prose, or error output.
evidence: Current code already enum-sanitizes next_action, wait kinds, item states, stages (partial), candidates (partial), and write_health summary_code — incomplete for mode/run ids/fingerprints/operation id/staleness/advance_run_id.
Prior canary suite seeded forbidden fields (tokens/prompts) but not public-capable scalars — revised contract requires full scalar canary matrix (challenge 47297690).
openspec/.../design.md Decision 3 intent (allowlist over denylist); this revision tightens value-level validation.
decisions.generalization_boundary: Does not sanitize or redefine non-factory-status surfaces (audit, logs, evidence bundles, scoreboard). Exception detail stays in process logs, not the remote envelope. Identifier patterns are intentionally lossy for remote safety.
decisions.uncertainty: Low on the remote-safety requirement. Medium that identifier max-length/pattern will need a few additive tweaks as real engine pin / treatment fingerprint formats appear; additives stay pattern-compatible within schema_version "1".

decisions.title: Independent heartbeat with concurrent async refresh, monotonic merge persistence, and identity-bound durable failure marker
decisions.surface: core/scripts/factory-status.ts (`DEFAULT_INDEPENDENT_HEARTBEAT_MS`, `startIndependentHeartbeat`, failure-marker reader); core/scripts/loop/supervisor.ts (`driveSupervisor` wiring, `markControllerOperation`, independent heartbeat); process fields in core/scripts/loop/types.ts; durable failure-marker seam distinct from process-identity record

alternatives.option: Keep only cycle-end heartbeat refresh
alternatives.rejected_because: Long blocking whole-item dispatch stalls cycle-bound refresh and makes a live process look dead; acceptance requires independent cadence during dispatch/wait/backoff.

alternatives.option: Infer liveness solely from model/worker progress messages
alternatives.rejected_because: Acceptance forbids requiring model/worker progress messages for heartbeat advance.

alternatives.option: Share `recoverySleep` for independent heartbeat sleeps
alternatives.rejected_because: Would couple recovery-backoff accounting/tests to liveness cadence; supervisor explicitly separates the channels.

alternatives.option: Full-record heartbeat write from a stale getRecord snapshot without versioning (prior d4)
alternatives.rejected_because: Concurrent operation/wait/progress/terminal writes can be overwritten by a delayed heartbeat snapshot (challenge 7c60ea85).

alternatives.option: Record heartbeat_write_error only in-memory or only on the failed process-identity write
alternatives.rejected_because: A failed process-record write cannot durably publish its own failure; status on another process can still see a prior fresh heartbeat_at (challenge 39e18c4b).

alternatives.option: Unbounded failure markers without identity binding or recovery clear (unspecified lifecycle)
alternatives.rejected_because: A stale marker from a prior boot can falsely degrade a replacement controller after successful heartbeats (challenge 35a49bf7).

alternatives.option: Require a dedicated OS thread/process for heartbeat independent of the Node event loop
alternatives.rejected_because: Production dispatch is Promise-based harness wait and yields the event loop; concurrent async heartbeat is sufficient.

assumptions: Controller holds the run lock and owns process-identity persistence while driving.
Default wall-clock interval of 15s is an acceptable production bound; tests inject shorter intervals and sleeps.
`dispatchItem` and other long controller waits are async (Promise) and yield the Node event loop during child/I/O wait.
A durable failure-marker path can succeed when the process-identity write path fails, or marker failure is itself observable as non-healthy.
invariants: Heartbeat refreshes on bounded independent cadence without model progress messages.
Independent heartbeat is a concurrent async task started before the cycle/dispatch loop (`startIndependentHeartbeat` + injectable sleep).
Refresh stops after lock loss / terminal exit (`shouldContinue` / `stop()`).
Persistence protocol (monotonic merge, not blind full-record replace from a stale snapshot):
- Process-identity record carries a monotonic `record_version` (or equivalent CAS generation) incremented on every successful durable write.
- Operation/wait/progress/lock-loss/terminal writers always write the full intentional field set and bump version.

- Heartbeat writer performs identity-bound merge: re-read latest record immediately before write; apply only `heartbeat_at` (and clear same-identity write-error) when `run_id`, `boot_id`, and lock `token` still match the driving identity and the controller is not terminal; refuse to write if version moved mid-flight unless the merge is rebased onto the newer version; never copy a stale operation/wait/progress/terminal snapshot over a newer one.
- Terminal stop / lock loss sets a durable terminal or driving=false condition; subsequent heartbeat merges MUST no-op and MUST NOT revive a stopped controller record.
- Interleaving unit tests inject delayed/reordered writes for heartbeat vs dispatch/wait vs failure vs terminal and prove no lost operation fields and no post-terminal revival.
Durable failure-marker schema (side channel, not only in-memory):
- Fields: schema_version, run_id, boot_id, hostname, pid, failed_at (ISO), error_code (allowlisted only).

- Written after process-identity heartbeat/operation write failure; best-effort; if marker write also fails, status must not report healthy solely from a within-bound prior heartbeat when independent refresh is overdue (unknown/write_failed policy).
- Status honors a marker only when it binds to the exact controller instance under observation (run_id + boot_id match the process-identity record being classified).

- Recovery clear: a successful process-identity write by that same run_id+boot_id clears/supersedes the marker (delete or overwrite with cleared generation). A replacement controller with a new boot_id ignores prior markers for other boot_ids.

- Stale markers: if process-identity shows a successful heartbeat_at newer than marker.failed_at for the same boot_id, ignore marker; if marker boot_id is absent from current process record (restart), ignore marker.
- Restart tests cover: marker from dead boot does not degrade new boot after successful heartbeat; same-boot marker after write failure degrades status; cleared after recovery write.
evidence: Current startIndependentHeartbeat spreads full `base` then overwrites heartbeat_at and writeProcess(next) — racy vs markControllerOperation full-record writes (supervisor.ts); revised by monotonic merge protocol.
Failure marker lifecycle was named in prior d4 but schema/binding/clear were unspecified — revised for challenge 35a49bf7.
openspec/.../specs/controller-independent-health/spec.md: independent cadence and failed-persistence requirements.
decisions.generalization_boundary: Wired on the durable loop supervisor path first; #890 macro-controller must use the same writer + marker seams when it is the exclusive drive owner (see d6/d8). Not a cross-host liveness claim. Not a multi-threaded runtime redesign.
decisions.uncertainty: Medium on 15s default vs write contention; medium on exact store CAS primitive (dedicated record_version field vs store-level generation) — implementation may pick either if interleaving tests pass. Low on concurrent-async sufficiency for Promise-based dispatch.

decisions.title: Three independent health dimensions; dead is recorded-identity death with same-host absence and replacement-safe unknown
decisions.surface: core/scripts/factory-status.ts (`classifyFactoryHealth`, probes: `isPidAlive`, optional `isServiceActive`, identity hostname/pid/boot_id/service_controller, lock/process correlation); public JSON `health` block

alternatives.option: Single boolean "alive" / "stuck" conflating wait and wedge
alternatives.rejected_because: Acceptance requires process liveness, durable progress, and expected waiting as separable dimensions.

alternatives.option: Classify stuck from wall-clock age of last event alone
alternatives.rejected_because: Creates false positives on long legal waits (CI, provider cooldown, backoff, capacity, human).

alternatives.option: Classify dead from stale heartbeat alone, including cross-host holders
alternatives.rejected_because: Single-host process evidence cannot prove remote death; design and concurrency scope forbid cross-host death claims.

alternatives.option: Classify dead from stale heartbeat + recorded pid-absent alone, including unmanaged same-host restarts (prior d5)
alternatives.rejected_because: A replacement unmanaged controller on the same host leaves the old pid absent while the factory is live; declaring factory-wide dead is a false positive (challenge 9447538d).

assumptions: Process identity authoritative binding is (hostname, pid, boot_id, run_id) on the process-identity record; optional service identity is service_controller when macro/service-managed.
Same-host hostname match is required before any local process/service probe is trusted for death.
Operations used for stuck detection are explicitly started with both start time and deadline recorded.
Liveness bound default 90s is the freshness window for independent heartbeats.
Public coarse `dead` means the recorded controller identity is dead, not a global claim that no factory controller exists on the host.
invariants: `suspected_stuck` requires live liveness AND explicitly started operation past deadline AND no durable progress since operation start AND not healthy waiting before a wait deadline.

`dead` (recorded identity) requires ALL of: (1) heartbeat stale/absent past bound for that identity, (2) same-host hostname match, (3) identity-bound absence proof for the recorded pid/boot/service instance, (4) no replacement evidence for the same run_id on the same host.

Replacement evidence (any one => not factory-live-dead; prefer `unknown` for coarse when the observed record is stale but a successor may exist): lockSummary shows holder_present for the same run with a different pid/boot; a fresher process-identity for the same run_id with different boot_id is present; service_controller is active while recorded pid is absent.

Unmanaged (no service identity): stale + pid-absent + same-host + NO replacement evidence => coarse `dead` with detail code `recorded_identity_absent` (documented as recorded-identity death). If replacement evidence exists => `unknown` (not dead).

Service-managed: running service with replaced process alone MUST NOT classify as `dead` -> `unknown` until new identity is observed or service is stopped; service stopped + recorded identity absent may be `dead`.
PID reuse: pid-alive without binding that the live process is the recorded boot_id/controller instance is insufficient for `dead` and insufficient for healthy live upgrade from stale -> `unknown`.
Cross-host or insufficient evidence is `unknown`, never `dead`.
Expected wait with future deadline is healthy waiting, not stuck.
Heartbeat write failure (durable failure marker per d4, identity-bound) surfaces as non-healthy (`write_failed` / coarse `unknown`).

Classification matrix tests cover: stale+pid absent+no service+no replacement -> dead(recorded); stale+pid absent+replacement lock/process -> unknown; stale+pid absent+service active -> unknown; stale+pid alive (reuse) -> unknown; stale+service stopped -> dead when service identity present; cross-host -> unknown; probes unavailable -> unknown.
evidence: Prior classifyFactoryHealth upgraded stale->dead on same_host && pidAlive===false only — false-dead on unmanaged restart (challenge 9447538d).
LoopSupervisorProcess carries boot_id and run_id for restart/replacement distinction.
openspec/.../design.md Decision 5 and controller-independent-health dead/unknown scenarios; concurrency scope single-host only.
decisions.generalization_boundary: Does not authorize automated remediation from suspected_stuck/dead. Not a multi-host consensus health model. Service probe is host-local when service identity is present.
decisions.uncertainty: Medium on exact service-manager probe shape until #890 service records stabilize. Low on stuck/waiting rules (acceptance-locked). Low on recorded-identity semantics for dead once replacement evidence rules are implemented.

decisions.title: Shared ControllerHealthEvidenceWriter; owned expected-wait lifecycle; macro is identity-only until it implements the writer
decisions.surface: shared writer seam (mark operation/wait/progress + independent heartbeat + failure marker) implemented by loop supervisor now and required for #890 when macro is exclusive drive owner; core/scripts/loop/types.ts wait kinds; core/scripts/loop/supervisor.ts concrete call sites; factory-status readers

alternatives.option: Require a new mandatory process-identity schema version that rejects pre-#891 supervisor.json
alternatives.rejected_because: Acceptance requires legacy runs and missing optional sources remain readable with explicit unknown/legacy attribution.

alternatives.option: Store operation/wait evidence only in-memory or only in action-evidence free text
alternatives.rejected_because: Stuck classification needs durable start/deadline/progress timestamps independent of free text; free text is also forbidden on the remote-safe surface.

alternatives.option: Omit default dispatch deadline and only mark operations that callers specially configure
alternatives.rejected_because: Stuck classification cannot fire without an explicit deadline; long dispatches would remain unclassifiable forever.

alternatives.option: Only mark dispatch/recovery waits without named owners for other acceptance kinds
alternatives.rejected_because: Acceptance lists CI, provider cooldown, recovery backoff, dependency, capacity, and human waits as healthy-waiting categories.

alternatives.option: Defer macro-controller health ownership without a writer interface or explicit unknown fallback (prior d6/d8 gap)
alternatives.rejected_because: Challenge 5f0162e5: without a designed #890->#891 writer contract, macro-as-driver has no path to independent heartbeat/operation/wait evidence and status could misread identity-only macro fields as live health.

assumptions: Process-identity record remains the durable liveness/progress/wait evidence surface (distinct from lock token ownership).
Two-hour default dispatch operation deadline is a coarse backstop, not a product SLA.
Until #890 implements the writer, production may run hybrid: macro for identity/contract, loop supervisor as exclusive drive owner and health writer.
invariants: Optional fields load on older records without migration.

Shared interface `ControllerHealthEvidenceWriter` (name may vary) exposes: independent heartbeat start/stop with d4 merge protocol; `markControllerOperation` / wait set-clear; durable failure-marker write/clear; identity fields (run_id, boot_id, hostname, pid).
Loop supervisor implements the writer now and remains the health writer whenever it is the exclusive item driver (including hybrid #890 outer + loop inner).

When #890 macro-controller is the exclusive drive owner, it MUST implement the same writer and advance heartbeat/operation/wait during long dispatch and provider wait without relying on a loop-supervisor writer. Injected integration-style tests MUST prove that path with fakes of the #890 driver.

When macro source is present for identity only and processIdentity is absent or not written by any implementer, factory status MUST attribute process_liveness / operation / expected_waiting as `legacy` or `unknown` — never invent healthy live macro health from identity/mode/revision fields alone.
Owned wait writers and lifecycle (set -> hold with future deadline -> clear) without raw reason text:
- dispatch: set at whole-item dispatchItem start (operation dispatch_item + wait kind dispatch + default 2h deadline); clear on success/failure.
- recovery_backoff: set before recovery sleep chunks with deadline = now+min(retryAfter,60s); clear after sleep stretch.
- capacity: set on pure worktree capacity_wait / admission stop with future recheck deadline; clear when capacity clears or run stops.
- human: set on hold-outstanding / blocked_needs_human park with future check deadline; clear on resume/unblock/terminal.
- dependency: set when frontier is dependency-gated (not deadlock-stopped) with future recheck deadline; clear when eligibility unblocks or terminal.
- ci: set when in-flight item waits on CI with future deadline; clear on CI terminal or dispatch end.
- provider_cooldown: set when provider/rate-limit cooldown is the wait reason with cooldown_until as deadline; clear when cooldown ends.
Nested waits during an active dispatch MAY specialize expected_wait_kind/deadline while keeping dispatch operation id/start/deadline for stuck detection.
Absence of operation deadline cannot yield suspected_stuck from age alone.
Wait kinds on the public envelope are allowlisted only; no free-text reasons.
evidence: Loop supervisor already owns markControllerOperation + startIndependentHeartbeat for the drive path.
Prior design deferred macro health ownership to generalization_boundary without a falsifiable writer contract — revised for challenge 5f0162e5.
Types enumerate all wait kinds (loop/types.ts LoopExpectedWaitKind).
openspec/.../specs/durable-loop-supervisor/spec.md already allows supervisor to remain item driver when macro is outer owner — hybrid path is in-spec.
decisions.generalization_boundary: Does not implement #890 service control plane. Does not change lock ownership or advance-stage internal deadlines. Does not require campaign-specific (#654) progress ownership. Deadlock terminal stops are stop records, not expected waits.
decisions.uncertainty: Medium on exact default recheck deadlines for capacity/human/dependency/ci when upstream signals lack an explicit deadline — implementation MUST pick a bounded documented default per kind. Medium until #890 production drive ownership is stable; hybrid writer path is the supported interim.

decisions.title: Honest cost/telemetry tri-state; no quota or zero-cost invention
decisions.surface: core/scripts/factory-status.ts (`CostCoverageKind`, envelope `cost` block, provider source forbidding `remaining_quota_percent`)

alternatives.option: Emit 0 cost or 100% remaining quota when telemetry is missing for prettier dashboards
alternatives.rejected_because: Acceptance forbids remaining-quota percentage and zero-cost inference from absence; missing data must stay unknown.

alternatives.option: Omit the cost block entirely when data is missing
alternatives.rejected_because: Snapshot field checklist expects cost coverage present as actual/estimated/unknown with attribution rather than silent absence.

assumptions: Upstream cost sources, when present, already distinguish actual vs estimated vs unknown.
Provider cooldown is a separate boolean/deadline signal, not a quota percentage.
invariants: Cost coverage is only `actual` | `estimated` | `unknown`.
Assembler does not invent remaining-quota percentages or zero USD from missing sources.
evidence: core/scripts/factory-status.ts: `CostCoverageKind`, `FactoryCostSource` / `FactoryProviderSource` comments forbidding remaining_quota_percent.
openspec/.../design.md Decision 6.
Issue acceptance criteria and proposal honesty section.
decisions.generalization_boundary: Does not implement a cost accounting system; only projects allowlisted coverage fields when provided.
decisions.uncertainty: Low. Falsified if a later product requirement mandates inventing synthetic cost/quota and contradicts this issue.

decisions.title: Graceful #890 absence: loop supervisor primary writer when macro missing or identity-only
decisions.surface: core/scripts/factory-status.ts (`FactoryMacroControllerSource` optional, controller.kind macro|loop_supervisor|unknown, run/controller attribution); CLI assembly path; health writer ownership rules in d6

alternatives.option: Block #891 until #890 macro-controller is always present in production
alternatives.rejected_because: Issue depends on #890 for full identity but acceptance requires readable status with explicit unknown/legacy for missing optional controller fields.

alternatives.option: Invent synthetic macro-controller identity when none is running
alternatives.rejected_because: Design Decision 7 forbids inventing a macro-controller that is not running.

alternatives.option: Treat macro identity fields as sufficient health evidence without a writer
alternatives.rejected_because: Would report live/healthy without independent heartbeat/operation/wait evidence (challenge 5f0162e5).

assumptions: Narrow #890-shaped interface is sufficient to fill identity/mode/revision/contract when present.
Loop supervisor process identity + durable loop status remain available for pre-#890 and hybrid deployments.
